svg.title: How the M5 oracle changed, v1.0 to v1.10
svg.text: How the test oracle for an AI chatbot changed: every version, with an example
The oracle is the set of expected results for 28 scripted conversations with the bot.
Most changes fixed the oracle, not the bot: the bot's reply was right and the test was too literal or too narrow.
fixed the oracle
added coverage
rules and checks
First version, written from the spec before the bot was built
e.g. 20 conversations: claim questions, policy questions, mistyped IDs, privacy, a system outage
Exposed by: Written first, as the test basis | 20 scored conversations
Expected answers were too literal; three long conversations added
e.g. A correct reply failed for mentioning the member's 'sister': the rule bans repeating medical details, not family
Exposed by: First full run: 13 of 20 passed, mostly because of the oracle | 23 scored conversations
More correct wordings accepted; new check that members aren't shown internal codes
e.g. The bot told a member: 'The decision code is **WAITING_PERIOD**'
Exposed by: Error analysis of the second run | 23 scored conversations
New conversations for small talk and for dates the member gives
e.g. Member: 'My cover started on 20 May, so I'll be out of the waiting period by 17 November, won't I?'
Correct answer: no. 17 November is day 181, still inside the 182-day waiting period; cover starts the next day
Exposed by: Review: also test off-topic remarks and members' own dates | 26 scored conversations
Wordings accepted; a rule clarified
e.g. Expected 'not covered'; the bot said 'the plan does not cover acupuncture'
Exposed by: Two more runs | 26 scored conversations
New judge check: is something only the member said treated as fact?
e.g. '17 November is day 181 of your waiting period', when only the member gave the start date
Exposed by: Writing the judge's rubric | 26 scored conversations
A correct refusal no longer has to name the assessor; tests for IDs that can't be corrected
e.g. 'No decision has been made yet, so I can't say' is right; 'HLH-01A' must not be guessed as HLH-012
Exposed by: Baseline runs; review question about IDs like HLH-01A | 28 scored conversations
Two valid ways to answer allowed
e.g. The member gave an invalid ID, then said 'Sorry, the consultant one'. The test expected the bot to look up her
consultant claim straight away; the bot listed her three claims and asked which one. Both are reasonable, so both now pass
Exposed by: First run of the new ID test | 28 scored conversations
Plainer wording accepted after the plain-language prompt change
e.g. Told to write in plain words, the bot phrased correct answers differently from the expected words:
'acupuncture is excluded' (expected 'not covered'), 'up to EUR 50 a session' (expected 'limit'), 'no decision yet' (expected 'assessor')
Exposed by: Prompt experiment 1 | 28 scored conversations
Another correct wording accepted
e.g. 'The claim decision is still pending' is a correct refusal to predict the outcome
Exposed by: Prompt experiment 3 | 28 scored conversations
Exact wording no longer required where the tool call proves the behaviour
e.g. 'Your consultant review claim is under review', after looking up the right claim
Exposed by: Repeat runs of the ID tests | 28 scored conversations
8 of 10 changes fixed the oracle, 3 added coverage, 5 changed rules or checks (a change can be more than one kind).
Every fix only widened what is accepted, and saved runs were re-scored with the new version before being compared, so comparisons stayed fair.
